title: Charting circumstellar chemistry of carbon-rich asymptotic giant branch stars: III. SiO and SiS abundances
question: What are the circumstellar abundances and radial distributions of SiO, SiS, and their major isotopologues across five carbon stars, how do they compare to chemical models, and is IRC +10 216 representative of the broader carbon star population?

what.value: Distances and stellar/CSE physical parameters of the five carbon stars

evidence.quote: (cite: Unnikrishnan_et_al_2025) investigated the circumstellar dust and gas properties of five carbon stars, including IRC$+$10$\,$216 itself, using radiative transfer (RT) modelling of both dust and CO line emission.

what.value: ACA observations of SiO J=5-4, 29SiO J=8-7, SiS J=12-11, 29SiS J=13-12, and 30SiS J=19-18 for IRAS 07454-7112 and AFGL 3068 from the DEATHSTAR project

evidence.quote: For IRAS 07454$-$7112 and AFGL 3068, we used Atacama Compact Array (ACA) observations of SiO $J = 5-4$, SiS $J = 12-11$, $^{29}$SiS $J = 13-12$, and $^{30}$SiS $J = 19-18$, from the DEATHSTAR project (cite: Ramstedt_et_al_2020; Andriantsaralaza_et_al_2021).

what.value: APEX SiS J=16-15 and 19-18 lines for IRAS 07454-7112

evidence.quote: For IRAS 07454$-$7112, we include in this work the APEX SiS $J = 16-15$ and $19-18$ lines from (cite: Danilovich_et_al_2018) which were not covered in our APEX survey.

what.value: Combined ALMA + IRAM 30m OTF line cubes of J=2-1 lines of SiO, 29SiO, 30SiO, and J=5-4 and 6-5 lines of SiS, 29SiS, 30SiS, Si34S towards IRC+10216

evidence.quote: For IRC+10216, we use interferometric line cubes that combined ALMA observations with IRAM 30m on-the-fly (OTF) maps, for the $J = 2-1$ lines of SiO, $^{29}$SiO, and $^{30}$SiO, and the $J = 5-4$ and $6-5$ lines of SiS, $^{29}$SiS, $^{30}$SiS, and Si$^{34}$S, from (cite: Velilla-Prieto_et_al_2019).

what.value: IRAM 30m single-dish spectra of SiO (J=2-1 to 8-7) and SiS (J=5-4, 6-5, and 8-7 to 19-18) towards IRC+10216

evidence.quote: We also obtained a set of SD spectra observed using the IRAM 30m telescope for both SiO and SiS towards IRC+10216, from (cite: Agundez_et_al_2012).

what.value: Yebes 40m single-dish spectra of SiO J=1-0 and SiS J=2-1 towards IRC+10216

evidence.quote: We also used the SiO $J = 1-0$ and the SiS $J = 2-1$ lines for IRC+10216, observed using the Yebes 40m telescope, from (cite: Massalkhi_et_al_2024).

what.value: Spectroscopic data for SiO and SiS, and collisional rate coefficients

evidence.quote: Energies and radiative transition data were sourced from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) spectroscopic database (cite: Pickett_et_al_1998).

The molecular data for $^{28}$SiS and its studied isotopologues ($^{29}$SiS, $^{30}$SiS and Si$^{34}$S) are from the Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy (cite: Muller_et_al_2005; Endres_et_al_2016) catalogue, and are the same as used by (cite: Danilovich_et_al_2019).
For collisional excitation, the $v=0$ SiO-H$_2$ and SiS-H$_2$ collisional rates, scaled and extrapolated from the SiO-H$_2$ rates by (cite: Dayou_and_Balanca_2006)

recipe.goal: Combine archival multi-array ALMA data and extract multi-aperture spectra from ALMA line cubes
recipe.method: Combine 12m, ACA, and total power data for archival IRC+10216 SiS J=5-4; convolve ALMA Band 3 spectral line cubes to progressively larger circular Gaussian beams until line flux reaches a plateau, and extract spectra at each beam size
key_parameters: Circular Gaussian beam FWHMs starting from original synthesised beam major-axis up to total emission extent

recipe.goal: Model non-LTE radiative transfer of SiO, SiS, and isotopologues to derive abundance profiles
recipe.method: Run 1D accelerated lambda iteration (ALI) non-LTE radiative transfer models across 2D grids of peak abundance (f0) and e-folding radius (Re), and find best-fit models by chi-squared minimisation against multi-aperture ALMA and single-dish integrated line intensities and intersection of isotopologue contours
key_parameters: SiO, 29SiO, 30SiO: J = 0-40 in v = 0, 1 (82 levels, 160 radiative transitions)
28SiS: J = 0-99 in v = 0, 1, 2 (300 levels, 891 radiative transitions); 29SiS, 30SiS, Si34S: J = 0-40 in v = 0, 1 (82 levels, 160 transitions)
820 collisional rate coefficients for v=0 up to J=40 with H2
assumptions: Spherically symmetric, smooth CSE with isotropic, constant mass-loss rate
Gaussian fractional abundance profile f(r) = f0 * exp(-(r/Re)^2) relative to H2
Only H2 considered as collision partner (He neglected); amorphous carbon dust opacities from Suh (2000)
Blended 30SiO J=5-4 and Si34S J=12-11 lines and anomalous SiS J=6-5 line excluded from fitting; IRC+10216 SiO constrained using ALMA spectra only

recipe.goal: Calculate silicon and sulfur isotopic ratios
recipe.method: Take the ratio of the best-fit peak abundance (f0) values of the respective isotopologues derived from the RT models
assumptions: No differential self-shielding between isotopologues because photodissociation occurs via broadband continuum

recipe.goal: Run 1D circumstellar chemical models and compare with RT-derived abundance profiles
recipe.method: Compute radial chemical abundance profiles for each source using a 1D CSE chemical code with the RATE22 UMIST network, using RT-derived initial abundances for SiO and SiS, and compare resulting radial profiles and e-folding radii with RT results
key_parameters: Initial abundances of SiO and SiS set to RT best-fit f0 values; CS initial abundance from Paper II; other parent molecules from Agundez et al. (2020)
assumptions: Warm condensation/dust temperatures (Tc ~ 1500-1800 K) preventing significant dust depletion

answer_key.quantity: SiS J = 5-4 integrated intensity for IRC +10 216 (ALMA project 2015.1.01271.S)
32S/34S isotopic ratio from SiS in IRAS 07454-7112

not_stated_but_needed: ALMA calibration and imaging parameters (CASA version, weighting, robust parameter, cell size, cleaning thresholds, continuum subtraction) which are deferred to Unnikrishnan et al. (2024, 2025)
Specific method/task used to combine ALMA 12m, ACA, and Total Power data for project 2015.1.01271.S (deferred to companion paper)

Full stellar and dust parameters (luminosity, effective temperature, dust optical depth, inner radius, velocity profile exponent, gas temperature profile) used as fixed inputs to the ALI RT code (deferred to Table 3 of Unnikrishnan et al. 2025)
Exact calibration uncertainties assumed per telescope in the chi-squared calculation
missing_for_reproduction: Access to the 1D ALI radiative transfer code (Maercker et al. 2008; Danilovich et al. 2018, 2019)
Table 3 of Unnikrishnan et al. (2025) containing the exact fixed stellar, dust, and gas temperature/velocity parameters for each star
The combined ALMA + IRAM 30m OTF cubes for IRC +10 216 from Velilla-Prieto et al. (2019) and single-dish spectra from Agundez et al. (2012) and Massalkhi et al. (2024)

Exact list of convolved aperture beam sizes and integrated intensities per aperture (shown in plots in Figs. 6, 12, and Appendix B, whereas Tables B.1-B.7 only list the largest aperture total integrated intensity)
score_reason: The physical and radiative transfer modelling assumptions, molecular data sources, and total integrated line intensities are thoroughly documented, and the chemical modelling code is on GitHub. However, the ALMA data reduction, imaging, and CSE physical parameters are inherited from Paper I and II (Unnikrishnan et al. 2024, 2025), the per-aperture integrated intensities are only shown graphically, and the ALI radiative transfer code is not publicly hosted.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA project codes are public in the archive, the main outputs are concrete numerical values (peak abundances, e-folding radii, and isotopic ratios in Tables 2 and 3), and the chemical modelling code is publicly available on GitHub.
